articles.title: Catal Capital Lends $38M on Margaritaville-Branded RV Resort in Georgia
articles.narrative: A joint venture between South Street Partners and Brighton Real Estate Ventures secured $38 million in construction financing from Catal Capital for the development of a Margaritaville-branded RV resort in Brunswick, GA. The project, Camp Margaritaville Resort Golden Isles RV, will feature 341 spaces and is expected to be completed in early 2028. The lender noted the growing institutional maturity of outdoor hospitality, driven by demand for experience-driven stays, and expressed confidence in the sponsors' vision.

data_points.property_name: Camp Margaritaville Resort Golden Isles RV
data_points.notable_features: The resort will feature 56 casitas and 285 RV pads, along with amenities including a swimming pool, restaurant, bar, clubhouse with retail, fitness center, pickleball courts, dog park, music pavilion, and boathouse.

articles.title: Sports Clothing Brand RBX Direct Signs 5K-SF Garment District Lease
articles.narrative: RBX Direct, an activewear brand, has signed a lease for 4,800 square feet of office and showroom space at 102 West 38th Street in Manhattan's Garment District. The transaction reflects the landlord's strategy of securing tenants that align with the building's overall tenant mix and support business growth.

data_points.address: 102 West 38th Street, New York City, NY

articles.title: For Mall Giant Macerich, More Turnaround in Q3
articles.narrative: Mall owner Macerich reported improved financial performance in the third quarter of 2026, with net operating income and revenue increasing year-over-year, signaling progress in its "Path Forward Plan." The REIT's net loss significantly narrowed compared to the previous year, and funds from operations also saw a notable rise. Leasing activity was robust, with 1.2 million square feet of leases secured and a 1.5% increase in portfolio occupancy, reaching 94.9%. The company continues to execute its disposition strategy, including the recent sale of Pacific View Mall, and anticipates a new mall acquisition by year-end.

data_points.notable_features: Portfolio consists of 37 assets, with a 'Go Forward' portfolio concentrated in California, Pacific Northwest, Phoenix, D.C., New York areas, and North Carolina.

articles.title: Get to Know the Broker: Michael Martirena of Compass
articles.narrative: This article profiles Michael Martirena, a luxury residential real estate advisor at Compass, highlighting his career achievements and personal insights. Martirena, part of the Ivan & Mike Team, specializes in high-net-worth client transactions across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties in Florida. He closed $298.32 million in sales in 2025 and has surpassed $2 billion in career sales. Martirena emphasizes the importance of consistency, market knowledge, and building a business that can thrive independently.

articles.title: The Co-op Comeback: New York Buyers Are Reconsidering the Condo Trade-Off
articles.narrative: New York City's residential market is seeing a resurgence in co-op appeal as buyers reconsider the long-standing preference for condominiums. The increasing cost of new condo developments, coupled with the significant price advantage of co-ops, is driving this shift. Some co-op boards are also adapting by streamlining application processes and easing subletting restrictions, addressing historical concerns that made co-ops less attractive. This trend is particularly noticeable in the luxury market, where Manhattan co-ops recently surpassed condos in sales for the first time since 2022, indicating a broader market re-evaluation of the co-op trade-off.

articles.title: Provident Industrial Completes 497,280 SF Project in El Paso
articles.narrative: Provident Industrial, a subsidiary of Provident, has completed the fourth and final phase of Gateway Logistics Park in El Paso, Texas. This phase adds three rear-load industrial buildings totaling 497,280 square feet to the park. The completion brings the entire Gateway Logistics Park to approximately 1.4 million square feet across six buildings, enhancing the region's industrial capacity.

data_points.notable_features: Consists of three rear-load buildings (Buildings 4, 5, and 6). Buildings 4 and 5 each span 147,420 square feet with a shared 205-foot truck court. Building 6 totals 202,440 square feet with a 130-foot truck court and 44 trailer parking stalls.
data_points.project_notes: Construction of Phase IV began in spring 2025. This is the fourth and final phase of the park.

articles.title: LaSalle Acquires Stake in CityWest Office Campus in West Houston
articles.narrative: LaSalle Investment Management has acquired an undisclosed equity stake in CityWest, a four-building, 1.5 million-square-foot office campus in West Houston. The property, originally purpose-built as a corporate headquarters, was 98 percent leased at the time of the recapitalization. This acquisition was made in a joint venture with investment firm 3Edgewood.

data_points.notable_features: Purpose-built corporate headquarters campus; amenities include a recently renovated fitness center, basketball court, multiple dining venues, and outdoor gathering areas.

articles.title: STRIVE Arranges Sale of Small-Bay Industrial Property in Plano
articles.narrative: STRIVE has arranged the sale of a small-bay industrial property located at 4400 Tradition Trail in Plano, Texas. The transaction details, including the buyer and sale price, were not disclosed. The property, built in 2022, features 24-foot clear heights.

articles.title: ULI Emerging Trends Report: Manhattan, Jersey City, Among Top 10 Markets to Watch in 2027
articles.market: New York City, NY / Jersey City, NJ
articles.narrative: The annual Emerging Trends in Real Estate 2027 report, a collaboration between the Urban Land Institute (ULI) and PwC, identifies Manhattan and Jersey City as top markets to watch, ranking them 7th and 8th respectively. Manhattan's significant improvement from its 2022 ranking of 42nd is attributed to diversified strengthening across office, retail, and tourism sectors, bolstered by a substantial infrastructure pipeline. The report highlights AI companies as a key driver of office absorption in Manhattan, alongside planned office-to-residential conversions. Jersey City continues to be a strong performer due to its robust multifamily construction and its appeal as a more affordable, well-connected alternative to Manhattan.

articles.title: Colliers brokers sale of two industrial facilities in Columbus market
articles.narrative: A private investor has acquired two Class-A industrial facilities totaling 404,088 square feet in the Columbus, Ohio metropolitan area. The properties, located in Canal Winchester and Commercial Point, were developed by Tenby Partners in 2023 and were fully leased at the time of sale. The transactions underscore the sustained investor demand for modern industrial assets in Central Ohio, driven by robust transportation infrastructure and access to key distribution corridors.

data_points.notable_features: Both properties benefit from strategic locations within Central Ohio's industrial corridors, offering connectivity to the regional interstate network and major freight infrastructure, including proximity to Rickenbacker International Airport, the Rickenbacker Inland Port, and the Norfolk Southern Intermodal Terminal.

articles.market_intelligence: Central Ohio continues to attract industrial investment, supported by established transportation infrastructure and ongoing regional development.

articles.title: Big-D Midwest wraps construction of second phase of affordable-housing community in Woodbury
articles.narrative: Big-D Midwest has completed the second phase of Settler's Ridge, an affordable housing community in Woodbury, Minnesota. This phase adds 126 residential units, mirroring the design and amenities of the first phase. The units are offered at various Area Median Income (AMI) levels to ensure affordability.

data_points.notable_features: Units feature balconies, granite countertops, stainless steel appliances, walk-in closets, and in-unit washer/dryer. Community amenities include a fitness center, club room, playground, dog park, outdoor grill stations, heated underground parking, and EV charging stations.
data_points.project_notes: Units are offered at 50%, 60%, and 70% of the Area Median Income (AMI).

articles.title: Cushman & Wakefield brokers sale of former public works facility in O’Fallon
articles.narrative: Cushman & Wakefield brokered the sale of the former City of O'Fallon Public Works facility, a 37,002-square-foot industrial property on 5.57 acres, to Earthworks Inc. for $4,400,500. The property, comprising two industrial buildings with warehouse, office, and service space, along with secured outdoor storage, is strategically located in the growing St. Charles County industrial market. The sale occurred after the City of O'Fallon relocated its operations, allowing the new owner to reposition the asset for continued industrial or contractor-oriented uses.

data_points.notable_features: Property consists of two industrial buildings with warehouse, office, service space, and secured outdoor storage areas.
data_points.project_notes: The property previously served as the City of O'Fallon's public works operations center before the city relocated to a new facility.

articles.title: Farmington Hills’ Farbman Group makes two hires, one promotion
Cushman & Wakefield takes over 7.5-million-square-foot property management portfolio in Louisville market
articles.narrative: Cushman & Wakefield has assumed management of a 7.5 million-square-foot portfolio of industrial, office, and retail properties in Louisville, KY, previously managed by NAI Fortis Group. This transition significantly expands Cushman & Wakefield's regional property management footprint to approximately 20 million square feet. The move was prompted by the planned retirement of NAI Fortis Group's founder and president, Jon Seiz, who sought to ensure continuity for clients and opportunities for his team, six of whom have joined Cushman & Wakefield.

data_points.project_notes: The portfolio transition was prompted by the planned retirement of NAI Fortis Group founder and President Jon Seiz.

articles.title: Continental Buys 125K-SF Centennial Shopping Center
articles.narrative: Continental Realty Corporation has acquired the 125,000-square-foot Quebec Village Shopping Center in Centennial, CO, for $31 million. This transaction marks CRC's second retail acquisition in the Denver metropolitan area, expanding its regional presence. The property includes a significant vacant anchor space, offering future repositioning opportunities.

articles.title: ARCO Breaks Ground on 355K-SF Advanced Manufacturing Facility in Maryland
articles.narrative: ARCO Design/Build has broken ground on a 355,000-square-foot advanced manufacturing facility in Hagerstown, Maryland, for Jamison Door Company and its parent company, BMP Group. This project represents the initial phase of a larger 58-acre North American manufacturing campus, aiming to enhance production capacity and integrate U.S.-based manufacturing for European brands. The first phase is slated for completion in Q1 2028, with further expansion already being planned.

data_points.notable_features: Advanced manufacturing facility designed to bolster growth and add U.S.-based manufacturing for European brands.
data_points.project_notes: This is the first phase of a planned 58-acre North American manufacturing campus. Planning for a second phase is underway.

articles.title: Cross Harbor Scores $78.5M Financing for Tempe Rental Community
articles.narrative: CrossHarbor Capital Partners secured $78.5 million in construction take-out financing for The Alyssa, a 335-unit Class A multifamily community in Tempe, Arizona. The property, delivered in 2024, achieved stabilization within 18 months, demonstrating strong market performance. The financing was arranged by JLL's Capital Markets Debt Advisory team.

data_points.notable_features: Class A community with studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom floor plans; amenities include a swimming pool, outdoor lounge, Peloton-equipped fitness center, co-working lounge, and controlled-access parking garage with EV charging stations.

articles.title: Thor Equities Closes on $218M Manhattan Office Buy
articles.narrative: Thor Equities Group has acquired 1359 Broadway, a 22-story, 486,000-square-foot office building in Manhattan's Garment District, from Empire State Realty Trust for $217.5 million. This acquisition reinforces Thor's confidence in the long-term strength of the Manhattan market and adds a significant asset to its portfolio, building on the property's established position in Midtown. Newmark will handle the exclusive leasing for the property.

data_points.notable_features: Features upgrades such as a new lobby with a restored original ceiling and a diverse tenant mix.

articles.title: Data Center Industry Reckons With New Roadblocks After Electoral Wipeout
articles.narrative: The data center industry is facing new challenges following significant Democratic midterm election victories, which were partly fueled by public opposition to data center development. This shift in the political landscape suggests potential roadblocks for future projects and operations within the sector.

articles.title: 13 GW At Immediate Risk As Texas Data Center Developers Face New Power Struggle
articles.narrative: The national political shift is anticipated to decelerate the development of data centers across the United States, with Texas, currently leading in data center construction, expected to be significantly impacted. This slowdown could affect a substantial amount of planned data center capacity in the state.

articles.title: From Waterfront Development To City Charters: How South Florida Voted On Local CRE Ballot Measures
articles.narrative: South Florida voters recently decided on 10 local ballot measures that will have direct implications for commercial real estate development and policy across the region. These measures covered a range of issues, from specific waterfront development projects to broader changes in city charters, reflecting the community's engagement with urban planning and growth.

articles.title: Cushman & Wakefield's Global HQ Sells At 45% Discount
articles.narrative: An affiliate of Prime Finance, in a joint venture with Hines, has acquired the 31-story office tower located at 225 W. Wacker Drive. The transaction for the global headquarters of Cushman & Wakefield closed at a significant discount.

articles.title: Brookfield Gives Up DTLA's Beaudry Apartment Tower
articles.narrative: Brookfield has opted to surrender the Beaudry apartment tower in downtown Los Angeles rather than refinance the four-year-old high-rise. This decision has led the lenders to begin marketing the loan for sale, indicating a significant shift in the property's ownership and financial structure.
